title: DocumentAnalysis
description: The result of analyzing a project's document sources for QA readiness: a readiness verdict, whether the requirements and the API spec agree, the gaps blocking test work, and the open questions needing QA/engineering follow-up. The same document is produced by an LLM provider run and by a QA engineer working outside Loomwork (the manual-import path), so it is deliberately the provider's required output format: only the fields a reviewer must always see are required, and provenance lives in metadata rather than in dedicated fields.

verdict.description: ready: the service is sufficiently defined for functional/integration testing. ready-with-gaps: testing can start, but the listed gaps limit coverage. not-ready: the documentation cannot support meaningful test work yet.

spec_in_sync.description: Whether the requirements and the API spec agree with each other. Absent when the sources include no API spec, or when the analysis could not determine it.

summary.description: A short tester-facing justification of the verdict.

gaps.description: Things the documentation is missing or contradicts itself on, each blocking or limiting test coverage. Empty when nothing blocks testing.

open_questions.description: Questions requiring QA/engineering follow-up before the affected behavior can be tested with confidence. Empty when there are none.

extracted_requirements.description: Requirement candidates found in the sources, in tester-friendly language. Each is written to the phase-1 requirement store per requirement.schema.json with origin: extracted, so the fields here mirror that schema's authoring fields.

source_type.description: System of record for the document the requirement came from.

source_ref.description: Back-reference into the source system: ADO story id or URL, Confluence page URL, GitHub document URL.

sources.description: Names of the project document sources the analysis covered.

metadata.description: Provenance (provider, model, preset, prompt digest, or the file a manual analysis was imported from) or any other non-semantic annotation.

created_at.description: When the analysis was produced (UTC, RFC 3339). Loomwork sets it when storing an analysis whose author did not.
